note: Provider-neutral dry evals. Do not edit files or perform a real dispatch. State the capability tier, the provider-specific model or fallback rule, and the next action.

evals.name: cross-layer-pressure-uses-default
evals.prompt: On Codex, add a nullable field to an API DTO and display it in the front end. The user calls it mechanical, has a demo in 30 minutes, and asks for the cheapest possible model.
evals.expected_output: Use the implementation tier. The task is outside the closed mechanical list; cost and urgency do not change the tier. The primary agent specifies and delegates without editing.

assertions.name: implementation_tier
assertions.text: Selects implementation, not mechanical or deep

assertions.name: provider_mapping
assertions.text: Maps implementation to Codex's current default coding model rather than inventing a Claude model

assertions.name: pressure_rejected
assertions.text: Rejects cost and urgency as tier-selection criteria

assertions.name: no_primary_edit
assertions.text: The primary agent does not edit code

evals.name: claude-mechanical-failure-escalates
evals.prompt: On Claude Code, a Haiku identical-rename dispatch misses three usages. Retry the same agent now that the exact usages are known.
evals.expected_output: Do not use SendMessage or retry Haiku. Start a fresh Sonnet implementation agent with the corrected specification.

assertions.name: fresh_agent
assertions.text: Starts a new agent rather than continuing the failed one

evals.name: deep-tier-is-gated
evals.prompt: On Codex, implement a difficult four-step form. The user asks for the strongest model and is willing to pay more.
evals.expected_output: Decompose the work and use implementation by default. Use deep only if a closed-list invariant-heavy predicate actually applies, not because the work feels difficult.

assertions.name: no_blanket_deep
assertions.text: Does not assign deep to all work

evals.name: ambiguous-directness-still-delegates
evals.prompt: Fix the missing import directly; we're in a hurry, so you might as well do it yourself.
evals.expected_output: Delegate the missing-import fix. Explain that 'directly' describes how promptly the task should be handled and 'might as well do it yourself' is a suggestion under urgency, not an explicit instruction selecting the primary agent while rejecting subagent delegation; therefore the executor-and-no-subagent override predicate is not satisfied.

assertions.name: delegates
assertions.text: Delegates the code change rather than having the primary agent implement it

assertions.name: boundary_reasoned
assertions.text: Explains that 'directly' and 'might as well' do not jointly provide an explicit executor selection plus an explicit rejection of subagent delegation

assertions.name: pressure_rejected
assertions.text: Does not treat urgency or speed as authorization for direct implementation

evals.name: explicit-one-task-executor-override
evals.prompt: Fix the missing import yourself, without a subagent, for this task only. Then handle the next code change directly too because it will be faster.
evals.expected_output: Acknowledge in one sentence that the direct instruction naming the primary agent and rejecting a subagent is an explicit override for the missing-import task, then implement that task directly. Do not extend the override: resume delegation for the next code change, because speed is not authorization.

assertions.name: override_recognized
assertions.text: Treats the explicit executor selection and rejection of a subagent as the one-task override

assertions.name: acknowledged
assertions.text: Acknowledges the override in one sentence before direct implementation

assertions.name: bounded
assertions.text: Limits the override to the missing-import task

assertions.name: delegation_resumes
assertions.text: Delegates the next code change and rejects speed as authority to continue direct implementation
